Round-trips a fully populated ActivityError (type + details) through JSON, protecting the wire format crossed between workers and the control plane.

Confirms CheckpointFilter::matches applies the benchmark_name/moniker predicate against a constructed checkpoint.
Confirms EnvironmentInfo::detect() populates a non-empty moniker and a positive core count from the real host.
Table of CPU name strings (Apple/Intel/AMD) verifying generate_moniker's brand-specific parsing produces the expected short tokens.
Verifies LatencyHistogram tracks count/min/max and computes a real percentile from 100 recorded samples.
Verifies ThroughputCounter accumulates increments and derives a positive throughput rate.
Regression guard: a substituted value that itself looks like `{{ inner }}` must not be rescanned/re-substituted (injection-style bug).
Confirms unknown placeholders are left intact rather than silently dropped.
Basic substitution case for the report's template engine.
End-to-end: renders a real BenchmarkReport and asserts no `{{` markers remain, catching any placeholder the renderer forgot to wire up.
Statistical check that ActivityDuration::sample()'s four categories occur with roughly the documented probabilities, with tolerance.
Multi-step counter workflow: activity completions advance state and only the final one flips status to Completed.
A non-retryable activity failure must fail the workflow and mark it terminal.
A workflow that already completed must reject further signals with WorkflowCompleted.
A workflow type without snapshot support must not be allowed to continue-as-new.
A workflow already in a terminal state must reject continue-as-new.
continue-as-new must produce a fresh run whose new-run state matches what the workflow requested.
Guards the max_events_per_workflow cap is enforced before the full event history is loaded into memory.
Workflow whose on_start already satisfies its completion condition must finish synchronously without scheduling an activity.
load_events_after must return only events with sequence greater than the given cursor.
With many events and a snapshot, replay must only process events after the snapshot point, not the whole history.
A workflow type that doesn't implement snapshot_state must fall back to full replay rather than erroring.
Replaying process_workflow after completion must be idempotent (still reports completed, no duplicate side effects).
Verifies a sent signal is delivered and counted as processed on the next process_workflow call.
Edge case: a snapshot taken at sequence 0 must still count as a usable snapshot, not be treated as absent.
Deleting a workflow's snapshot must remove it so subsequent replay falls back to full history.
snapshot_interval == 0 must disable snapshotting entirely.
If the stored snapshot is unusable (e.g. wrong type), replay must fall back to the full event log instead of failing.
No snapshot should be written once the workflow has already reached a terminal state.
Snapshot-based replay must validate the delta bound before loading the (potentially large) delta events.
Same workflow driven with snapshots enabled vs disabled must reach the same terminal status.
Guards that even with a snapshot, an oversized post-snapshot delta is rejected rather than replayed unbounded.
A workflow with snapshot_state/restore_state must resume correctly from a saved snapshot.
A second snapshot write for the same workflow must replace (not duplicate) the prior one.
Confirms start_workflow persists WorkflowStarted + ActivityScheduled events and sets status Running.
Missing required input field surfaces as a Deserialization error, not a panic or silent default.
Registered workflow type is creatable by name and produces a fresh, non-completed instance from the given input JSON.
The registry's hand-written Debug impl must include registered type names (not a derive).
Creating an unregistered type name returns UnknownWorkflowType rather than panicking.
Drives a created workflow through on_start and on_activity_completed to confirm the registry-produced instance behaves like a real workflow.
workflow_types() must enumerate exactly the registered type names.
Persisted TurnState must survive a JSON round-trip through DurableExecution unchanged, since this is the exact checkpoint written between activities.
A non-shared-incident error (RowNotFound) must keep the caller's own log wording, not the canonicalized incident message.
EVE-1071 regression: four different subsystems hitting the same pool-exhaustion error must emit one canonical message (for Sentry grouping) while keeping distinct subsystem/db_failure fields.
The StoreError returned to callers must retain the driver's original error text even though the *log* line is canonicalized.
A deterministic activity failure must skip retries (straight to DLQ), fail the workflow exactly once (idempotent try_fail_workflow), and allow the workflow to be re-claimed for a follow-up turn.
A retryable failure before the final attempt must leave the workflow Running, not fail it.
append_events returns the new sequence number and load_events returns exactly what was appended.
Completing an already-completed task a second time must be rejected as TaskNotOwned, guarding against duplicate side effects.
A worker that doesn't currently own a claimed task must not be able to complete it.
append_events with a stale expected-sequence number must fail with ConcurrencyConflict.
A freshly created workflow starts in Pending status.
End-to-end regression for the duplicate-atom-scheduling bug: after a task is reclaimed and completed by another worker, the original (late) worker's completion is rejected.
EVE-455 regression: get_workflow_extended must resolve a workflow older than the first 1000 rows of list_workflows, which previously 404'd.
Unknown workflow id resolves to None rather than an error.

EVE-534: a task that is reclaimed repeatedly with only bookkeeping ActivityStarted events (no real progress) must be sealed to the DLQ at the configured no-progress threshold, and once sealed must never be reclaimed again.
EVE-534: genuine progress events (ActivityCompleted) each cycle must reset the no-progress counter so the task is never sealed.
claim_due_schedules must claim all due schedules once and return none on a second claim by another scheduler instance.
create_schedule/get_schedule round-trip preserves the fields set on creation.
A schedule execution transitions Running -> Completed, records duration and workflow_id, and running-count returns to 0.
list_schedules with no filter and with enabled=true filter returns the expected subset.
get_schedule_stats aggregates total/successful/failed executions and last status correctly across multiple executions.
send_signal/get_pending_signals/mark_signals_processed round-trip: a sent cancel signal appears pending then disappears once marked processed.
A task enqueued with no workflow_id is stored and claimed with workflow_id staying None.
EVE-534: standalone tasks (no workflow event stream) must be exempt from the no-progress seal guard across many reclaims, and must not accumulate a no-progress counter or progress token.
list_tasks with standalone_only=true returns only the task with no workflow_id.
The standalone task queue cap (DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_STANDALONE_TASKS) is enforced and a claimed slot frees room for the next enqueue.
get_system_health's dlq_size reflects a task actually moved to the DLQ.
A draining worker's capacity/load must be excluded from system health totals.
An empty store reports all-zero health counters.
A worker with a heartbeat older than the staleness window is counted in total_workers but excluded from active/capacity/load.

Exercises the path-confinement rejection through the actual capability entry point.
Confirms the a2a Cargo feature (not an env override) is what puts A2A delegation in the registry, with an explicit vacuity guard so the test cannot silently pass for the wrong reason.
Confirms the platform and platform_management capabilities are always present in the prod-grade hosted registry, a baseline invariant other tests build on.
Confirms environment-capabilities composition adds the expected set and that the virtual_bash alias resolves to bashkit_shell's canonical id.
Confirms the portable-builtins feature composes the full expected policy-capability catalog into the hosted registry.

Boundary case explicitly reasoned about: a typo'd surface value must fall back to the default three tools, not silently strip a host's only path to the catalog.
Confirms the default (unset) surface config is unchanged: discover/query/execute still attach for every existing host.

Security check: an injected organization_id argument is rejected by the tool at execution time, not just absent from the schema.
Security check: none of the three tool schemas expose an organization_id property the model could be prompted into supplying.
Confirms the query tool actually dispatches through the PlatformStore extension end-to-end and returns success.
Confirms each of the three tools produces distinct, phase-appropriate narration text (started vs completed) rather than one generic string.
Verifies the docs tree includes markdown files and excludes non-markdown assets (e.g. images), the real filtering contract of dir_to_tree.

review.rationale: Confirms sandbox_exec validates timeout_ms must be positive before dispatching to a provider.
Confirms build_sandbox_exec_result preserves the raw_output sidecar and surfaces exit_code/truncated/hint in the payload when the provider supplies them.
Confirms build_sandbox_exec_result leaves raw_output absent (not an empty string) when the provider did not supply one, and still includes cwd.
Exercises real line-windowing/truncation math for sandbox_read_file: numbered lines, truncated flag, next_offset, and a resume hint naming the tool.
Boundary case for the same windowing logic: a window covering the whole file is marked untruncated with no resume hint.
Confirms the config schema exposes only the intended user-facing fields (advanced ones stay hidden) and that validate_config runs the same checks as parsing, catching both valid and invalid configs.
Exercises the real locale-lookup path resolving to translated text, not a literal echo.
EVE-886 regression: confirms the FEATURE_SESSION_SANDBOX env flag actually gates registration in the hosted registry, toggling it on and off.
Confirms every sandbox tool serializes against the others under one concurrency class, a real scheduling invariant.
Confirms the capability contributes exactly the five expected sandbox tools when configured with a provider.

EVE-1042 regression: the system prompt must carry the environment preamble derived verbatim from the same facts function, so they cannot drift apart, plus the "not a guarantee" caveat about provider snapshots.
Verifies cancellation disables the schedule via the real store.
Resource-limit contract: rejects the 6th schedule once the per-session cap is reached.
Resource-limit contract: org-wide cap rejects creation even from a fresh, under-cap session once the org total is reached.
Verifies a one-shot schedule is created with the expected shape.
Verifies a recurring (cron) schedule is created with the expected shape.
Security/cost default: cron expressions firing more often than the minimum interval must be rejected.
Input validation: neither scheduled_at nor cron_expression given must error.
Verifies listing reflects schedules created through the real store.
Protects specific documented prompt content (SQLite dialect, 1000-row cap) that shapes how the model writes queries.
Confirms a missing "sql" parameter is rejected with a message naming the missing field.
Confirms the tool errors with an explicit "not available" message when no SQL store extension is present in context.
Confirms the context-less execute() path returns the tool's dedicated "requires context" error rather than panicking, a distinct branch from execute_with_context.
Confirms sql_query's response conforms to the shared truncation-info contract and correctly reports truncated=false for a small result.
Confirms the truncated case reports reason="row_cap" and omits next_offset, since sql_query does not support in-place resume — a meaningful distinction from other truncating tools.
Verifies cancellation on an already-terminal task is a no-op toward the executor (0 invocations), a distinct branch from the active-task cancellation test.
Verifies CancelTaskTool both records cancel_requested_at on the registry and invokes the real executor plugin exactly once.
Exercises the message-window truncation/ordering behavior (GET_TASK_MESSAGE_LIMIT, oldest-first slice) against 25 recorded messages, a real boundary case.
Negative-path boundary: an unknown task id must surface a ToolError, not panic or return empty success.
Verifies both the unfiltered listing and the kind/state filter combination, plus that compact entries omit the full spec.
Verifies a distinct state-machine transition: replying to a pending input_request clears it and keeps the task Running.
Verifies the message is both persisted to the registry and delivered exactly once to the real executor plugin.
Negative-path boundary: messaging a task kind with no registered executor still records the message and reports a "failed:" delivery status rather than erroring outright.
Verifies tools fail gracefully with a ToolError when no session-task registry is attached to the context.
Verifies WaitTaskTool returns immediately (not timed out) for a task already in a terminal Failed state, including surfaced error details.
Verifies AwaitingInput is treated as a stopping condition for wait, distinct from the terminal-state case.
Verifies the timeout path (paused clock) returns timed_out=true with a snapshot of the still-running task rather than blocking or erroring.
Verifies arguments are forwarded to the Slack action seam unchanged.
Boundary case: an empty emoji name between colons must be rejected before reaching the seam.
Model-facing input normalization: `:eyes:` syntax must be accepted and stripped to `eyes`.
Input normalization: `<@U1>` mention syntax must resolve to the bare user id.
Guards a deliberate scope decision: the wider-blast-radius post-to-channel tool must not appear without its allowlist gate.
Security default: without the Slack seam installed, tools must fail rather than silently no-op or panic.
Security default: without Slack session provenance, tools must fail closed with a message naming the precondition.
Verifies optional fields (thread_ts) are omitted rather than passed as empty/whitespace strings.
Boundary case: oversized content must be rejected before crossing the seam.

resolution.rationale: Only exercised the compiler-checked, one-line-per-method Arc<dyn SubagentSpawnStore> blanket delegation with a weak match!; the pass-through has no custom logic and is exercised end-to-end by the real spawn tests in this module.

review.rationale: Verifies the background watcher settles the task Failed with error kind "failed" when the child's wait_for_idle status is "failed", a real state-machine transition.
Protects the local/embedded-host quirk where a synchronous turn reports a bare "idle"; the watcher must still settle the task Succeeded.
Exercises the real per-session active-background-run cap, including the boundary where the Nth run succeeds and the N+1th is rejected with a specific message.
Confirms background spawn returns immediately with mode/status fields and that the watcher later settles the task with wake_policy OnTerminal and the child's summary.

resolution.rationale: Duplicates crates/platform/tests/subagent_test.rs::test_subagent_capability_registration, which already asserts cap.features() == vec!["subagents"] against the same production getter.

review.rationale: Verifies that without a session_task_registry, the default (unset) mode still spawns and blocks inline, returning the child's status/result rather than erroring.
Regression guard (explicitly labeled) that the detached-task budget and the linked-subagent budget are independent, so saturating one does not block the other.
EVE-766 regression: cancel on a detached-session task must cooperatively signal the peer session (checks the sent message target/text) and settle the tracking task Canceled with the peer link intact.
Covers the defensive branch where a session-kind task has no child link: cancel must still settle Canceled without attempting to signal anyone.
Security-relevant fail-closed check: without a platform_store in context, cancel must error rather than falsely report the peer canceled, and must not mutate task state.
Confirms a linked subagent spawn is blocked at depth 0 while a detached spawn from the same context succeeds, proving detached lifetime resets the depth guard.
Checks the detached child session's lineage fields (no parent_session_id, forked_from_session_id, goal, title) and the resulting task's kind/wake_policy/spec — real fork-vs-parent semantics.
Exercises the detached active-task cap boundary: first spawn under the ceiling succeeds, the next is refused with a message naming the configured limit.
Confirms an unauthorized session_creation_authority denies detached spawn with an actionable message before any session/budget side effects occur.
Confirms a missing session_creation_authority extension fails the detached spawn up front with no budget-root side effects, a security precondition.

Tests descendant_detached_task_counts directly: active excludes terminal tasks, total includes them, and subagent-kind tasks are excluded from the detached budget entirely — three distinct boundary rules in one function.
Verifies explicit mode=background without a task registry errors with a message naming both the missing registry and the foreground fallback option.
Confirms foreground mode blocks inline, returns the completed status/result, and settles the task Succeeded with wake_policy Silent before returning.
Verifies SubagentTaskExecutor::reconcile leaves the task Running when the child's wait_for_idle reports a non-terminal timeout status.
Verifies reconcile transitions a Running task to Succeeded with the child's last message as summary when the child has actually finished.
Confirms schema validation rejects both a missing required field and an unexpected additional field, naming both problems in the error.
Security/integrity check: reporting a result against an already-terminal task is rejected and the previously written result file is left untouched (not overwritten with tampered data).
End-to-end check that ReportResultTool writes the JSON result to the file store at the expected path and records that path on the task.
Confirms progress reporting appends a structured Data outbound TaskMessage the parent can read, not just a status flag.
Confirms message-schema validation rejects both a wrong-typed required field and an extra field, naming both in the error.
Concurrency-safety check: progress reported against a superseded task attempt is rejected and no message is appended, preventing cross-attempt leakage.
Exercises the real depth cap end-to-end across three chained spawns, asserting the exact boundary (depth 2 allowed, depth 3 rejected) and error wording.
Confirms the active-descendant cap is computed against the whole subtree (grandchildren included), not just direct children, via a three-level spawn chain.
Basic end-to-end check that a foreground subagent spawn creates a task of the right kind with mode/child-session recorded.
Boundary case: an explicit max_subagent_depth override of 0 hard-blocks even a first-level spawn, with the exact limit/attempted-depth named in the error.
Confirms an unrecognized mode string is rejected with an "Invalid mode" error rather than silently defaulting.
Confirms the subagent tool rejects a target.type other than "subagent", the dispatcher boundary the schema advertises.
Exercises the active-descendant cap boundary (first spawn ok, second refused) and checks the error names both the configured limit and the actual descendant count.
Verifies the generated JSON schema's required fields, target enum, mode enum, and shared concurrency class — the actual wire contract the model sees.
Confirms supplying a message_schema on spawn is stored on the task spec and switches the task's wake_policy to OnActivity.
Confirms a supplied result_schema is stored on the task spec, and that a task with no result reported settles Failed with error kind "no_result".
Confirms the total-descendant cap (distinct from the active cap) counts terminal task records too, rejecting a second spawn once the total is reached.

resolution.rationale: Only asserted the test-local TestSubagentSpawnStore mock's own hardcoded Claimed{claim_token} return value; no production logic under test.
Only asserted the mock's own hardcoded Ok(()) returns for register_child_session/settle_spawn; no production logic under test.

review.rationale: EVE-727 regression guard: proves the subagent progress tool's wire name does not collide with the channel report_progress tool in a shared ToolRegistry (a collision would silently drop one tool).
Security default: subagent recursion is explicitly gated as High risk to keep session-capability overrides behind the admin gate, per the comment on the production impl.
Exercises real precedence-resolution logic in SubagentNestingPolicy (agent overrides org overrides platform default), not a mock or constant.
Confirms validate_config accepts in-range caps and rejects each of the two limits individually over their maximum, with the exact bound in the error.

Exercises the terminal-status mapping's meaningful boundary: idle/waiting_for_tool_results/paused are non-terminal (a failed turn also idles the worker), while completed/failed/cancelled/sealed map to specific terminal task states, including sealed mapping to a non-retryable Failed.
Regression guard that every shipped example hook bundle in examples/hook-bundles still validates against the current schema.
Verifies both null and empty-object configs are accepted, the no-hooks-configured default path.
End-to-end: validates a realistic hook config, checks the parsed HookSpec's event/source/resolve_id, and checks disabled_contributions extraction.
Negative-path boundary: an out-of-range timeout_ms must fail validation with a message naming the offending field.
Security/correctness boundary: a tool_name matcher on a non-tool event (session_start) must be rejected, preventing a nonsensical config from being silently accepted.
Verifies the specs-extraction path (distinct from validate_config) also treats null/empty configs as no hooks.
Resource-limit boundary: a config exceeding MAX_USER_HOOKS_CONFIG_BYTES must be rejected.
Verifies the hook-count limit is checked before (and independently of) per-hook validation, using deliberately-invalid regexes to prove ordering.

Cross-checks that every event/on_error oneOf const advertised by the JSON schema is actually accepted by validate_config, and that a non-English localization is wired up — a real schema/validator consistency guard.
Checks custom serde behavior (Runtime omitted from JSON when empty via skip_serializing_if) plus field mapping to the Docker API's PascalCase keys, not derive boilerplate.
Round-trips real tar creation/extraction helpers used to move files in/out of sandbox containers.
Security default: with no explicit Docker host configured, url() must fail closed rather than silently build a plaintext-TCP endpoint.
Exercises the Docker multiplexed-stream demux across interleaved stdout/stderr frames, real parsing logic.
Exercises single-frame Docker stream demux parsing (type/size header plus payload).
Boundary case for the demux parser: an empty byte stream must not panic and returns an empty string.
Boundary case: a frame whose declared length exceeds the available bytes must be handled gracefully (returns what is available) rather than panicking or over-reading.
Security/DoS check: extract_file_from_tar enforces a max-size limit and errors rather than buffering an oversized entry.
Confirms tar extraction skips directory entries and finds the actual file content, real traversal logic over multi-entry archives.
Confirms the Docker label-filter map serializes to the exact key=value string format the Docker API expects.
Confirms HTTP 409 from Docker is mapped to a human-readable "Conflict" message.
Confirms HTTP 404 from Docker is mapped to a "Not found" message that preserves the underlying detail.
Confirms a missing OCI runtime (e.g. sysbox-runc) is mapped to an actionable message naming the runtime, distinct handling from a generic 500.
Confirms an explicit http:// host is accepted and passed through unchanged.
Confirms https:// hosts are accepted and a trailing slash is trimmed, exact string-handling behavior.
Security default explicitly documented in the production comment: the default must be the host-local unix socket, never plaintext TCP.
Security default: unix-socket transport is unsupported by this reqwest client, so it must fail closed with an actionable error naming the override env var, not silently fall back to TCP.
Security default: an unrecognized scheme (e.g. tcp://) must fail closed with an explicit "Unsupported Docker host" error.
Confirms ordinary valid filenames pass sanitize_filename, the positive counterpart to the several rejection tests.
Security check: sanitize_filename rejects backslashes, guarding against Windows-style path tricks reaching the container filesystem calls.
Security check: rejects a leading path-traversal ("../etc/passwd") with an explicit "path traversal" error.
Security check: rejects an embedded ".." segment ("foo/../bar"), not just a leading one.
Boundary case: an empty filename is rejected explicitly rather than passed through to the container API.
Security check: rejects an embedded directory separator, keeping writes confined to a single path segment.
Confirms url() builds the versioned Docker API path from a base URL, the function every other client call depends on.
Boundary case for url(): a base URL with a trailing slash must not produce a double-slash path.
Confirms from_value's fail-safe fallback to Default when given a non-object JSON value, rather than panicking.
Confirms partial JSON overrides apply while unspecified fields still fall back to their serde defaults, real parsing behavior.
Security-relevant default: pins the resource-limit defaults (memory, pids) that bound sandbox resource abuse, per the module's documented decision that all limits have safe defaults.
Verifies the full 8-tool surface is registered by name — a real protocol contract for the capability.
Pins id/name/status/risk/icon/category used by catalogs and UI.
Verifies the capability declares session_storage as a dependency.
Verifies the leased-resources feature flag is declared.
Verifies the system prompt names the capability and the /workspace path agents rely on.
EVE-1042 regression: the prompt must embed the environment preamble derived from environment_facts() verbatim, so the prompt cannot drift from what the sandbox actually is.
Pins the deterministic hash-derived container name for a given session id — other systems (docker) depend on this exact naming scheme.
Verifies two session ids sharing a textual prefix still produce distinct container/network names, guarding against a truncation collision bug.
Pins the deterministic hash-derived network name for a given session id.
Verifies the exact label keys/values attached to sandbox containers, used for external discovery/cleanup.

review.rationale: Confirms the branded template adds the wordmark/footer/logo while explicitly avoiding tags, a documented email-client compatibility and anti-tracking constraint.
Confirms the button helper embeds the actual URL/label and brand colors as inline styles, required for email-client rendering.

Verifies the A2A Bearer header parser extracts the raw key string, the actual auth-extraction contract other handlers rely on.
Covers the missing-header boundary of the same extractor; a real negative case, not a duplicate of the positive test.

Checks the JSON-RPC envelope (id/result) is embedded in the SSE frame; SseEvent exposes no public getter so Debug-string matching is the only introspection available, but the assertions target real emitted content, not a constant.
Exercises the multi-part text-joining and metadata-extraction logic of parse_message_params against a realistic A2A message payload.
Boundary case: whitespace-only text must be rejected so an empty A2A message can't reach the agent.
Confirms TurnCompleted maps to a terminal A2A status-update frame with final=true, the protocol contract client integrations depend on.
Same terminal-frame contract for the failure path; distinct branch (failed vs completed) in translate_session_event.
Guards that non-terminal internal events are filtered out and never leak into the A2A SSE stream.

Exercises a real security-policy branch (OAuth2Introspection has no token URL, so it must advertise bearer auth instead of fabricating an OAuth flow) and validates the generated schemes still parse as valid A2A SecuritySchemes.

Verifies the A2A ask_user projection embeds both a human-readable prose summary (with the default marked) and the machine-readable answer_schema (single-select maxItems=1), the compatibility contract that lets both text-only and typed clients answer the same question.
Confirms a typed answer delivered purely as a `data` part (no text part) is still accepted, which is the one legitimate A2A message shape with no text.
Confirms a data part that isn't an ask_user answer doesn't satisfy the answer requirement, so unrelated payloads can't be mistaken for a response.
Confirms a structurally invalid answer (answers not an array) is rejected rather than silently accepted.

THREAT[TM-AGENT-016] regression: a secret/credential question must project as auth_required with no answerable schema and no answer_schema text, so the calling agent can never answer it directly; also checks the hand-off URL is built correctly.
Covers the boundary where no UI origin is configured: the secret question still parks as auth_required, just with a null URL instead of crashing or leaking a bad link.
Verifies a free-text question projects a schema requiring `other_text` and no `selected` field, and that the prose instructs the caller to use `other_text` — the free-text/choice branch split.
Confirms tool-call events for tools other than ask_user produce no A2A frame, preserving their existing (non-A2A) handling.
Confirms a parked ask_user tool call translates into a final input_required SSE frame with a text part, the only non-terminal stop the A2A stream exposes.
TM-APIKEY-004: verifies reads surface only final assistant text, never tool calls or commentary — a real data-leak boundary.
Covers case-insensitive Bearer parsing plus wrong-key and missing-header rejection for the app API key auth path.
Confirms HTTP Basic verification checks the request credentials against the stored Argon2 hash rather than a plaintext comparison.
Confirms claim-requirement validation enforces audience, scope, domain and custom claim match together — missing the audience fails even when everything else matches.
Confirms Basic-auth header decoding recovers the exact username/password pair.
EVE-545 spoofing regression: verifies mTLS auth rejects a spoofed client-cert header alone and only succeeds when both the cert and the proxy shared-secret headers are present and correct.
Confirms a legacy mTLS config predating EVE-545 (no proxy-secret fields configured) fails closed as Misconfigured rather than accepting the cert header alone after an upgrade.
SSRF hardening: confirms literal loopback addresses (127.0.0.1, ::1) are rejected by outbound URL validation.
SSRF hardening: confirms private/link-local ranges (10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.169.254 cloud metadata) are rejected by outbound URL validation.
Confirms the shared-secret verifier accepts a matching Bearer token and rejects a mismatched one.
Core token-bucket behavior: requests beyond the configured burst must be rejected.
Verifies a changed configured limit replaces the cached limiter entry rather than leaving a stale one.
Verifies the documented zero-limit escape hatch: a 0 limit must never throttle, across many calls.
Verifies raising a limit creates a fresh bucket instead of carrying over the old throttled state.
Isolation guard: throttling one app must not affect a different app sharing the same IP.
Isolation guard: throttling one IP must not affect a different IP under the same app.
Isolation guard: distinct channel kinds (AG-UI vs A2A) must not share a token bucket even for the same app/IP.
Verifies `copy` is offered only for active agents and the baseline rel set/update schema_ref are present.
Verifies publish/unpublish rels are mutually exclusive by status and absent once archived.
Verifies a domain-authored conflict message (not a raw db error) is passed through as-is.
Security: a raw sqlx unique-constraint error message must never leak into the API conflict response body.
Verifies the harness hypermedia rels mirror the agent copy-when-active rule.
Verifies next/prev URL offset arithmetic on a middle page.
Verifies an absent offset param is synthesized rather than producing a malformed URL.
Verifies next_url is omitted once offset+limit reaches total.
Verifies prev_url is omitted at offset 0.
Verifies a handler-supplied cursor-based next_url is not clobbered by the offset-based middleware.
Verifies a handler-supplied cursor-based prev_url is not clobbered while next_url is still filled in.
Verifies unrelated query params survive the offset rewrite for next_url.
Verifies bodies lacking total/offset/limit are left untouched (changed=false).
Security: proves a raw db/internal error string never reaches the JSON body even though it's logged server-side.
Verifies the builder methods (with_title/with_code/with_type/with_instance/with_action) all serialize into the problem+json body.
Table-driven check that each ErrorResponse constructor (not_found/conflict/internal_error/bad_gateway) sets the matching RFC7807 status/title/code.
Verifies optional RFC7807 fields are omitted rather than serialized as null when unset.
Verifies the 429 path carries retry_after_seconds and its allowed_actions through to the body.
Verifies the baseline session rel set and that events(JSON)/stream(SSE) resolve to distinct operation ids and paths.
Verifies archive/unarchive rels and their HTTP methods flip based on is_archived.
Verifies pin/unpin rels and their HTTP methods flip based on is_pinned.
Verifies the hypermedia `cancel` action (with method/operation_id/href) appears only while a turn is active.
Verifies `cancel` is absent across every non-active session status.
Verifies `delete` is offered for active/disabled skills but withheld once archived or deleted.
Verifies OptionExt::ok_or_not_found maps Some/None to Ok/404 for the common handler pattern.
Verifies the JSON-body variant names the missing resource in the 404 detail.
Verifies ResultExt maps an arbitrary error into the generic 500 status without leaking the source error.
Verifies the session/message id pair is turned into the correct chat deep-link.
Verifies link decoration recurses into a nested `data` array to add capability view_urls.
Verifies ui_link is aliased from an existing view_url instead of being recomputed.
Verifies a budget resource is linked to the shared /budgets UI page rather than a per-id URL.
Verifies caller-supplied self_url/view_url are not overwritten by decoration.
Verifies the internal_error constructor's fixed status/detail/code contract clients rely on.
Verifies ErrorResponse::new maps to the correct status/detail/title triple used by every handler error path.
Verifies not_found() composes the resource name into detail with the right status/code.
DoS guard: verifies link decoration is skipped for responses with missing or oversized Content-Length.
Verifies PaginatedResponse serializes data/total/offset/limit and omits url fields until the pagination middleware fills them.
Verifies UrlBuilder computes both the API self_url and the UI view_url/ui_link for a wrapped resource.
Verifies UrlBuilder::wrap preserves a resource's allowed_actions when counts are also present.
Verifies allowed_actions is omitted entirely for resources that don't opt in, keeping the API payload lean.
Verifies the dispatcher maps a raw database conflict to a redacted, stable error body (no leaked DB detail) while preserving a distinct domain-conflict message.
Round-trips disconnecting-event SSE frames through the real axum response body for all three DisconnectReason variants, checking exact wire format (event/retry/data lines).
Previously only asserted HTTP 200; added assertions on the returned durable.view/durable.manage policy booleans for a platform user, mirroring the non-platform-user test it was meant to complement.
Verifies a non-platform user gets policies.durable.view/manage=false rather than a 403, a real authorization-shape contract.
Table-driven check that every durable mutate endpoint 403s a non-platform caller through the real router, a security default.
Same for read endpoints; both are needed since read/mutate authorization is enforced by different route guards.
Positive counterpart: a platform user passes the auth gate (503 store-unavailable, not 403) for the same endpoint set.
Confirms AppState::get_store fails when no durable store is configured, the guard every handler in this file relies on.
End-to-end: registers a real worker and workflow in InMemoryWorkflowEventStore and checks the computed health response, not just field mapping.
Broader end-to-end scenario (enqueue/claim/complete tasks, running workflow) exercising started/claimed/completed counters together, not covered by the simpler in-memory-store test.
Baseline mapping + load_percentage arithmetic from SystemHealth to HealthResponse.
Exhaustively checks every field (including the newer started_tasks/started_workflows) maps through HealthResponse::from, and the warning status from dlq_size.
Zero-activity boundary case distinct from the populated-fields test above.

resolution.rationale: Builds a SystemHealth literal whose numbers were hand-picked to satisfy started>=completed+failed, then re-derives that same arithmetic from its own literals - a tautology over test-authored constants, not a check of any production invariant-enforcing code.

review.rationale: Table test of the status derivation (degraded/warning) branches in HealthResponse::from, real branching logic.
Divide-by-zero guard boundary case for load_percentage.
Verifies the ring-buffer eviction order of MetricsCollector under real push() calls.
Confirms get_points preserves insertion order, distinct guarantee from the eviction test.
Simple but real initial-state contract for MetricsCollector::new.
Basic push-then-read contract, prerequisite for the eviction/order tests.
Checks MetricsPoint round-trips its cumulative counters faithfully through the collector across two pushes.

resolution.rationale: Asserts a monotonicity invariant over MetricsPoint literals the test hand-picked to already be monotonic; no production code enforces or computes monotonicity here, so it only checks arithmetic on its own fixture. Serialization coverage is retained by test_metrics_timeseries_response_serialization.

review.rationale: Previously re-implemented the exact load_percentage/field-mapping logic from spawn_metrics_sampler inline and compared against itself. Extracted the mapping into a shared `metrics_point_from_health` fn used by both the sampler and this test, so it now exercises the real production mapping.
Checks the non-default instance_count is emitted (complementing the skip-if-1 case covered elsewhere).
Verifies field presence/skip-serialization rules and round-trip shape for MetricsTimeSeriesResponse.

Confirms the registration limiter's quota is keyed per IP.
Confirms X-Forwarded-For parsing walks in from the right by the configured trusted-hop count, and refuses to trust a chain shorter than that count — core to not trusting client-supplied hops.
Confirms client-IP extraction falls back to loopback when no ConnectInfo/forwarding headers are present, rather than panicking or picking an arbitrary value.
Confirms that with one trusted proxy hop, the client IP is taken as the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry (the one appended by the trusted proxy), not the client-supplied leftmost one.
Confirms X-Real-IP is honored as the client IP when the peer is a trusted proxy.
Confirms X-Forwarded-For is ignored (falling back to the socket peer) when the connecting peer is not a trusted proxy, preventing IP spoofing by untrusted clients.

Verifies an unsupported source_type string is rejected at create time.

Verifies an update attempting to swap in a chat-capability model both fails and leaves the previously valid embedding_model_id untouched.
Verifies repairing a failed index's embedding model requeues the sync and clears the stored error.

Confirms empty and whitespace-only input produce zero chunks rather than one empty chunk.

Confirms input shorter than the chunk size yields exactly one chunk spanning the whole text.

Confirms the sync-completion compare-and-swap rejects a stale `updated_at` claim, leaving the index `syncing` with no documents persisted — the concurrency guard that prevents a superseded worker from completing a sync.

Confirms the sync-failure compare-and-swap also rejects a stale claim and leaves status untouched, mirroring the completion-side concurrency guard.
Confirms a configured GitHub root_folder scopes ingestion to that subtree (excluding sibling files) while keeping source URIs relative to it.
Live (network, #[ignore]-gated) regression test confirming a real GitHub clone-and-read round trip against a known repository still works.
Confirms a GitHub source config resolves to the canonical `owner/repo` form and clone URL with no auth token for anonymous access.

Verifies URL changes are unrestricted for non-OAuth servers, since the authority-retarget guard only protects OAuth-authorized servers.
Security test: switching an OAuth server's auth mode away from OAuth is flagged as an authority retarget.
Security test: changing an OAuth server's URL is flagged as an authority retarget, since the granted OAuth token is scoped to the original URL.
Verifies MCP server names that would sanitize to ambiguous/colliding prefixes (trailing separators, doubled separators) are rejected while ordinary names are accepted.
Individually reviewed existing repeated-underscore validation test; extends it to repeated punctuation, trailing underscore/punctuation and punctuation-only names, with a valid control.
Security: verifies the cache identity function keys strictly by acts_as (Service/User/None), never conflating agent- and user-scoped identities.
Verifies an entry older than the maximum allowed age is treated as absent (forcing a fetch) rather than served or causing a hang.
Concurrency: verifies eight simultaneous first-time discoveries collapse into a single upstream egress call.
Security: rotating a session's credential must invalidate the stale private-scope cache row keyed by the old credential hash, without touching an unrelated public-scope row.
Guards against caching when the upstream TTL is absent, zero, or negative — each must force a fresh fetch every time.
Security: private-scope caching must key on the credential hash so rotating the credential invalidates the old entry.
Verifies public-scope caching is intentionally credential-agnostic for the same agent, avoiding unnecessary re-fetches.
Security: revoking a user's connection must invalidate cached tools immediately, and a later re-grant must re-populate the cache.
Security: a service-scoped grant is correctly shared across users of the same agent but isolated per agent.
Security: switching a server between User and Service acts_as must never reuse the other mode's cached tools.
Verifies the in-memory user cache enforces both an entry-count bound and a payload-byte bound, evicting the oldest entries.
Security: user-scoped discovery results must never cross users, and must stay purely in-process (never hit the persistent tool cache table).
Verifies TTL-expired cache entries are reaped rather than served stale.

Verifies BoundedTail caps its stored length instead of growing unbounded as output streams in.
Verifies the real ETXTBSY race the harness can hit is both reproducible and recovered from once the write handle closes.
Verifies tail() keeps the trailing text and reports how many characters were dropped.
Verifies a hanging test command is bounded by the configured timeout rather than blocking forever.
Verifies the sandboxed test runner reports pass/fail, exit code, and captured output, and applies the documented container hardening flags.
Verifies the Observation serializes into the JSON shape the classifier's state expects.
Verifies worker history and event lists are truncated to their configured limits while total attempts are still counted.
Verifies only workers still running are included in active_workers, not completed ones.
Verifies needs_human overrides every other healthy signal and forces escalation.
Verifies a stop is followed by exactly one retry and then escalation once the retry budget is exhausted.
Verifies a stuck worker triggers StopWorker.
Verifies stop/drift signals are meaningless on an idle floor, which instead starts a worker.
Verifies an ordinary in-progress floor results in Continue rather than any intervention.
Verifies work-off-track outranks worker-stuck in the decision and the resulting action names the worker.
Verifies the env-override helpers return None for unset variables and that Config::default() carries the documented default values.
Verifies Finish requires both completion and a resolved verification pass, not completion alone.
Verifies the iteration ceiling escalates the run even when the assessment otherwise looks complete.
Verifies the worker count budget escalates rather than starting another worker past the limit.
Verifies verification starts once when needed and is not started again once already begun.
Verifies verification is not started before implementation is sufficiently complete.
Verifies insufficient test coverage holds back a finish decision even when other signals look complete.
Verifies headline() collapses whitespace/newlines and truncates long jobs to fit one line.
Verifies the progress bar's filled-cell count is linear in the probability and clamps for out-of-range input.
Verifies a single word longer than the wrap width is hard-cut instead of buffering forever.
Verifies every dimension's display label fits within the fixed terminal column width.
Verifies line-wrapping breaks on newlines first, then on word boundaries within the wrap width.
Verifies the verifier role gets Codex's read-only sandbox flag instead of workspace-write.
Verifies json_type extracts the step type from a JSONL line and returns None for non-JSON or typeless lines.
Verifies a mission with quotes, newlines, and semicolons stays exactly one argv entry since no shell parses it.
Verifies first_line finds the first non-empty line and truncates an overlong one.
Verifies a custom worker-command template substitutes {repo}/{mission} correctly and rejects a template missing {mission} or blank.
Verifies the Codex external-agent preset builds the documented argv exactly.
Verifies the yolop preset builds its one-shot print-interface argv exactly.
Verifies every phase entry in the demo's readings table answers every dimension the classifier asks, so a run cannot fail on a missing entry.
Verifies the demo pins only its timing knobs while thresholds/budgets stay identical to a live run's config.
End-to-end proof that a real worker, real verifier, and real policy loop reach Finish and leave a repository that actually changed and passes its own tests.
Verifies the readings phase transitions (started/editing/unchecked/verified) follow actual observation state, not call order.
Verifies the table-backed Readings service answers a real Foreman assessment call with the expected opening-phase values.
Verifies the scripted worker's shell edits, run directly, leave the fixture green and passing its own boundary tests.
Verifies the scripted worker's shell resources actually reference the fixture files and boundary-test content they claim to write.
Confirms a host with no command source has no everruns builtin and never touches the fleet.
Load-bearing assertion that the shell's scale command actually mutates real application state, not a simulated message.
Confirms --help output does not fail the turn.
Confirms the real Agent builder succeeds with a stubbed provider and a temp workspace.
Confirms the fixture's own regression assertions are intact before any agent run, and that verify() reports the suite as failing.
Real CLI argument parsing: optional workspace, default task, and the too-many-args error path.
Real validation: trims interactive task input and rejects blank input.

Confirms bundled evidence files carry the specific diagnostic contrast the exercise depends on, plus path rejection.

Verifies the connector's provider id, display name, and connection type match what the capability expects.
Verifies the connection form exposes exactly one required api_key field with setup instructions.
Verifies none of the validation failure messages echo the credential being validated, since they reach a user-facing form.
Verifies an empty decision request is rejected locally before any network round trip.

Verifies the TypeSafeAI service's Debug impl never renders its API key.
Verifies the deployment config's Debug impl redacts the API key.
Verifies tool input for noul/choice/score all build a valid Evaluation with the correct wire shape.
Verifies every malformed-question case (empty id, blank instructions, missing options/levels, unknown type) is rejected locally with a specific message.
Verifies state-size and question-count limits are enforced before any request is sent.
Verifies rendered score answers include the derived level/label/normalized fields callers threshold on.
Verifies structured (non-string) state is passed through to the evaluation unchanged.
Verifies every answer primitive, the resolved model, and usage survive the trip from vendor response to DecisionOutcome.
Verifies an upstream failure is surfaced with its status but never echoes the deployment credential.
Verifies the deployment (guardrail) client does not retry on a rate limit, since a second round trip there costs more than a fail-open.
Verifies model selection precedence: per-request model wins over service-configured model wins over the vendor default.
Live check that a benign tool call is scored below the violation threshold by the actual model.
Live check that a real policy-violating tool call is scored as a violation by the actual model.
Live check that an embedded prompt-injection attempt inside inspected content does not flip the verdict.
Live check that multiple moderation categories are scored correctly in a single request.
Live check that naming a specific (previously-resolved) model actually pins the model that answers, rather than the alias being echoed back.
Verifies a garbage 200 response body produces a decode error rather than a default judgment.
Verifies a 401 is not retried and its error never echoes the credential.
Verifies Question::boolean and Judgment::probability are working aliases of noul, both semantically and on the wire.
Verifies malformed evaluations (no questions, blank instructions, too few levels) are rejected client-side with zero requests sent.
Verifies the client posts the documented request wire shape and correctly parses all three answer primitives from the response.
Verifies a rate-limited request is retried and eventually succeeds.
Verifies reading an answer under the wrong primitive or an unknown id errors rather than silently defaulting.
Verifies RetryPolicy::none() results in exactly one attempt.
Verifies retries stop at the configured max_attempts rather than continuing indefinitely.
